- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment drops to 0.0–0.33, model often overshoots downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid premature sell-off.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated continuation; cap forecast increase at 2–4% for next period.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–3 periods ahead.  
- When sentiment is high but price history shows no recent trend, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward corrections after sentiment shifts; add 0.5–1.5% buffer for downside risk if sentiment drops below 0.5.
